interactions.summary: A student offers J.K. Rowling as a test case and Jiang immediately doubles down that contemporary fame does not make someone a world-historical prophetic writer.

Students probe whether prophetic writers are predetermined, emptied vessels, differently filtered births, or products of suffering, while Jiang mostly lets the class elaborate the divine-channel model he has been building.

speaker_notes.note: The diarization labels this as a single speaker, but the opening 'Bruce? Thank you' suggests Jiang is calling on a student whose long answer follows.

claims.claim: Jiang flatly predicts that J.K. Rowling's contemporary prominence will not translate into the kind of century-scale readership he associates with prophetic writers who change history.
The student objection sharpens Jiang's frame by asking whether prophetic writers are determined in advance by God.
One student formulates good writing as emptiness or vesselhood: the writer becomes a channel for divine content instead of merely performing technique.
Another student extends Jiang's body-as-filter language and argues that some writers are born with filters that either distort celestial order or faithfully convey it to the secular world.
claims.temporal_scope: Student extension of lecture frame on 2026-06-26.

claims.claim: A further student resists Jiang's dismissal of Rowling by arguing that painful conditions and hardship can sharpen imagination and produce serious writing.

signature_moments.moment: The writer becomes a vessel only by emptying the self enough for the divine work to pass through.
signature_moments.source_phrase: you are very empty on the inside ... you are not a channel
signature_moments.why_it_matters: It compresses the lecture's writer-prophet theory into an ascetic practice of self-emptying rather than a marketplace or craft metric.

signature_moments.moment: A writer's body becomes a filter that either distorts celestial order or carries it into the secular world.
signature_moments.why_it_matters: It links Jiang's metaphysics of embodiment directly to literary vocation and failure.

glossary_terms.definition_or_usage: Student shorthand for the writer who transmits divine content rather than showing off technique.
The body's interpretive medium, which can either distort reality or convey divine order more faithfully.

chronology_notes.note: This packet shows students actively internalizing Jiang's June 26 writer-metaphysics and restating it in terms of vesselhood and bodily filtering rather than simple talent or fame.

uncertainty_notes.note: The student's Rowling/Hemingway example is syntactically noisy, so the summary captures the counterpoint about suffering and imagination without overcommitting to every biographical detail.
